checks.name: thrust needed to hover falls nearer the ground
checks.target: the lower one is the smaller
checks.note: the sign of the ground effect, which is all a two-height run can establish; ground_effect grades the magnitude on one disk

checks.name: the airframe is voxelised at all
checks.target: > 0, or the lattice cannot see the body
checks.note: a slab thinner than a cell passes between the nodes and voxelises to nothing, and the symptom is a wrench of exactly zero -- which reads as a coupling that is not wired up. At two cells per rotor radius this case measured 0 nodes for a 40 mm airframe on a 60 mm lattice

checks.name: fluid wrench on the airframe, as a fraction of weight
altitude settled
checks.measured: spread 0.057 R over the last third of the run
checks.target: < 0.1 R, which is what a stable loop looks like
checks.note: the graded property is that the loop is STABLE, not that it is accurate: a vehicle still oscillating is a coupling that has not settled, and a vehicle holding a wrong height steadily is a controller that has not been tuned

checks.name: altitude offset from target
checks.note: the size of the disturbance the controller had to reject, which is the ground effect it does not model. It is the measurement, not the error

checks.name: real time, simulated seconds per wall-clock second
checks.target: reported; the brief's 0.5x target is a device claim
